stem: Catch volumes vary widely but pressure was measured only at the pump. What additional evidence has highest value?
choices: Use the pump nameplate and pump discharge pressure together to estimate whether downstream delivery should be adequate.
Compare nutrient formulation and substrate dryback by location because large catch-volume differences can reflect plant demand as well as hydraulic performance.
Compare the previous crop's irrigation uniformity and yield data to determine whether the current pattern is new.
Measure representative downstream pressure and emitter output across near, far, and problem-prone positions and inspect filtration condition.
rationale: Pump pressure alone cannot show what pressure and flow actually reach emitters throughout the zone. Wide catch-volume variation calls for measurements where the problem occurs: representative downstream pressure, actual emitter output, line position, and filtration condition. Those data can identify pressure loss, restrictions, or localized delivery defects that a pump reading misses. Historical crop data and plant demand may add context, but they cannot replace direct verification of the current hydraulic distribution.
